## Grammar

Basic word order is SVO; it has prepositions. In the noun phrase: possessed before the possessor; noun before the adjective; noun before the demonstrative; numeral before the noun; noun before the relative clause. Overall it is head-initial.
It has no definite article, no indefinite article, no case marking on nouns, ergative-absolutive alignment, no grammatical number, no gender or noun classes.
Verbs mark past, future, progressive and habitual; there is an indirect (reported or inferred) evidential. Negation uses a negator before the verb; yes/no questions use a verb form. Verbs agree with the subject by suffixes; not with the object.
Other features: pronouns can be dropped; alienable and inalienable possession told apart; serial verbs; a copula; a periphrastic causative; a bound passive; question words moved to the front; a decimal counting base.
Measured morphology: 13 live grammatical markers, mean bondedness 1.0 (0 free word … 3 fused), 4 paradigm cells, 1 of them with allomorphy.

### Grammar sketch

Built from the typology and the live markers above (planet/language/sentences.py); where the engine tracks no marker for a construction, the form is the word such markers commonly grow from, and the text says so. Examples are glossed by the Leipzig rules (abbreviations under Sample sentences).

**Number.** Nouns do not mark number: one noun form serves for one or many; a numeral or 'many' says how many.

**Case.** Nouns have no bound case. Adpositions (free words, not yet case): locative (LOC): a separate word before the noun phrase (eje‼, from 'head'). The typology leans erg-abs in alignment, but no case marker shows it yet: word order tells subject from object.

| *eje‼* | *pele* |
| --- | --- |
| LOC | house |

‘in the house’

**Gender and noun classes.** There is no gender or noun class.

**Tense and aspect.** Verbs mark tense and aspect. Past (PST): a clitic before the verb (epe, from 'yesterday'); future (FUT): a clitic before the verb (ae, from 'want'); progressive (PROG): a clitic before the verb (e‼le‼, from 'walk'); habitual (HAB): a clitic before the verb (epe, from 'do'). Unmarked: perfective (left to context).

| *epe=paɛ* |
| --- |
| PST=go |

‘(it) went’

| *ae=paɛ* |
| --- |
| FUT=go |

‘(it) will go’

| *e‼le‼=paɛ* |
| --- |
| PROG=go |

‘(it) is going’

**Mood and evidentiality.** Speakers mark how they know: reported (evidential) (REP): a clitic before the verb phrase (ela, from 'say').

| *ela=paɛ* |
| --- |
| REP=go |

‘(it) goes, they say’

**Person agreement.** Verbs agree with the subject: 3SG: a clitic after the verb (pe, from 'he'). Subject pronouns are dropped when the marker is there. No marker yet for 1SG, 2SG, 1PL, 2PL, 3PL (zero).

| *paɛ=pe* |
| --- |
| go=3SG |

‘he/she goes’

**Negation.** Negation is a separate word before the verb phrase (tɛje, from 'nothing'); the typology calls it preverbal.

| *pe‼le‼* | *tɛje* | *elɛle‼* | *letɛjala* |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1SG | NEG | drink | milk |

‘I do not drink the milk.’ (sentence 6 below)

**Questions.** Yes/no questions use a marker on the verb. Question words move to the front: who te‼tae‼le‼, what ta, where ale‼ɛle‼, when taɛle‼, how e‼eta.

| *e‼* | *ta=je* | *ɛjaleje‼* |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2SG | Q=hear | thunder |

‘Do you hear the thunder?’ (sentence 4 below)

| *ta* | *tae‼le‼ȡa* | *ejapapɛ=pe* |
| --- | --- | --- |
| what | child | bring=3SG |

‘What does the child bring?’ (sentence 5 below)

**Possession.** The possessor stands after the possessed noun, with no marker. Kin and body parts (inalienable) take no genitive marker. 'Having' is said with 'with' ('my mother is with a dog'; the lane's pick for Grambank's 'neither').

| *jelelae* | *lete* |
| --- | --- |
| dog | man |

‘the man's dog’

| *elae* | *pe‼le‼* | *e‼je* | *jɛ* | *pelea* |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mother | 1SG | COP | with | boat |

‘My mother has a boat.’ (sentence 7 below)

**Relative clauses.** Relative clause after the noun, introduced by the word for 'that' (G055).

| *eje‼ejɛ* | *teja* | *ɛlɛle‼=pe* |
| --- | --- | --- |
| woman | REL | dance=3SG |

‘the woman who dances’

**Copula.** The copula is the word for 'he, she, it' (G056).

| *lete* | *teja* | *e‼je* | *pɛjate‼le* |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| man | that | COP | merchant |

‘That man is a merchant.’ (sentence 9 below)

| *a* | *e‼je* | *e‼eje* |
| --- | --- | --- |
| water | COP | cold |

‘the water is cold’

## Sample sentences

Built from this language's own words, word order, markers and agreement (planet/language/sentences.py). Each has the form line (‘-’ an affix boundary, ‘=’ a clitic boundary), a morpheme-by-morpheme gloss, the free translation, then the whole sentence in IPA (after the simple joining rules: a glide between two vowels, a nasal taking the place of a following stop) and in the book spelling. Nothing here is attested speech; it is what the grammar data implies.

**(1)** ‘The woman sees the dog.’

| *eje‼ejɛ* | *e‼a=pe* | *jelelae* |
| --- | --- | --- |
| woman | see=3SG | dog |

/eje‼ejɛ e‼ape jelelae/ · ‹Eyerheye erhape yelelae.›

<sub>SVO order; the verb carries the subject's 3SG marker</sub>

**(2)** ‘The big dog sleeps in the house.’

| *jelelae* | *wɛje‼* | *leje‼=pe* | *eje‼* | *pele* |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| dog | big | sleep=3SG | LOC | house |

/jelelae wɛje‼ leje‼pe eje‼ pele/ · ‹Yelelae weyerh leyerhpe eyerh pele.›

<sub>LOC is an adposition; adjective after the noun; the verb carries the subject's 3SG marker</sub>

**(3)** ‘The man built the boat.’

| *lete* | *epe=jeja=pe* | *pelea* |
| --- | --- | --- |
| man | PST=build=3SG | boat |

/lete epejejape pelea/ · ‹Lete epeyeyape pelea.›

<sub>PST is a clitic before the verb; the verb carries the subject's 3SG marker</sub>

**(4)** ‘Do you hear the thunder?’

| *e‼* | *ta=je* | *ɛjaleje‼* |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2SG | Q=hear | thunder |

/e‼ taje ɛjaleje‼/ · ‹Erh taye eyaleyerh?› · rising intonation

<sub>the verb takes a question clitic, cut down from the word for 'if, whether'; no question gram is tracked</sub>

**(5)** ‘What does the child bring?’

| *ta* | *tae‼le‼ȡa* | *ejapapɛ=pe* |
| --- | --- | --- |
| what | child | bring=3SG |

/ta tae‼le‼ȡa ejapapɛpe/ · ‹Ta taerhlerhďa eyapapepe?›

<sub>the question word moves to the front; the verb carries the subject's 3SG marker</sub>

**(6)** ‘I do not drink the milk.’

| *pe‼le‼* | *tɛje* | *elɛle‼* | *letɛjala* |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1SG | NEG | drink | milk |

/pe‼le‼ tɛje elɛle‼ letɛjala/ · ‹Perhlerh teye elelerh leteyala.›

<sub>negation is a free word (preverbal)</sub>

**(7)** ‘My mother has a boat.’

| *elae* | *pe‼le‼* | *e‼je* | *jɛ* | *pelea* |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| mother | 1SG | COP | with | boat |

/elae pe‼le‼ e‼je jɛ pelea/ · ‹Elae perhlerh erhye ye pelea.›

<sub>kin are inalienably possessed: the possessor stands beside the noun with no marker; possession with 'with' ('my mother (is) with a dog'; Grambank marks neither a 'have' verb nor locational possession, and the lane picked the conjunctional type); 'with' as a preposition (no COM gram)</sub>

**(8)** ‘My older brother catches three fish.’

| *lɛje‼atae* | *pe‼le‼* | *ele=pe* | *e‼le‼* | *ka* |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| older.brother | 1SG | catch=3SG | three | fish |

/lɛje‼atae pe‼le‼ elepe e‼le‼ ka/ · ‹Leyerhatae perhlerh elepe erhlerh ka.›

<sub>kin are inalienably possessed: the possessor stands beside the noun with no marker; numeral before the noun</sub>

**(9)** ‘That man is a merchant.’

| *lete* | *teja* | *e‼je* | *pɛjate‼le* |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| man | that | COP | merchant |

/lete teja e‼je pɛjate‼le/ · ‹Lete teya erhye peyaterhle.›

<sub>the copula is the word for 'he, she, it' (G056), in the verb's place (before the predicate); demonstrative after the noun</sub>

**(10)** ‘I know the woman who dances.’

| *pe‼le‼* | *ȶape* | *eje‼ejɛ* | *teja* | *ɛlɛle‼=pe* |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1SG | know | woman | REL | dance=3SG |

/pe‼le‼ ȶape eje‼ejɛ teja ɛlɛle‼pe/ · ‹Perhlerh ťape eyerheye teya elelerhpe.›

<sub>relative clause after the noun, introduced by the word for 'that' (G055)</sub>

Abbreviations: 1 first person; 2 second person; 3 third person; COP copula; LOC locative; NEG negation; PST past; Q question particle; REL relativizer; SG singular.

## Relatives and intelligibility

Shared-origin share: the share of core-100 meanings whose words go back to the same etymon (true cognates, and loans between the two). Intelligibility is the engine's estimate (blind cognates, how far the cognates have drifted, and grammar differences).
